448	          "subheadline": null,
449	          "body": "In 2018, founder Dani Reyes planted a single row of ghost peppers in her Chicago apartment's community garden plot. By August, she had more peppers than she knew what to do with. By September, she had a blender, a dozen mason jars, and a sauce that her neighbors described as 'aggressively good' and 'slightly dangerous.' By December, she was selling out of a folding table at the Logan Square Farmers Market every Saturday. Nobody was more surprised than Dani.\n\nLava Mouth wasn't planned. It was grown. The early sauces were made in a rented commercial kitchen from midnight to 4am, labeled by hand at the kitchen table, and sold from the back of a hatchback. Every batch was an experiment. Most were brilliant. A few were spectacular failures that have been sworn to secrecy.\n\nThe name came from Dani's nephew, who tried the original ghost pepper sauce at age nine and announced \u2014 with tears streaming down his face \u2014 that his mouth felt like lava. 513	          "headline": "Flavor First. Heat Second. Always Small-Batch.",
514	          "subheadline": null,
515	          "body": "A lot of hot sauce brands are in the business of pain. We're in the business of flavor. The heat is real \u2014 sometimes brutally so \u2014 but every Lava Mouth sauce is built around a flavor profile first. The pepper comes second. That's the rule Dani set in 2018 and it hasn't changed.\n\nSmall-batch isn't a marketing phrase for us. It's a hard cap. Every run is 500 bottles or fewer. That means we can adjust recipes based on how the peppers are tasting that season. It means we can try new things without betting the whole company on them. It means every bottle you open is the result of someone's actual attention, not a formula running on autopilot.\n\nWe source our peppers from three family farms \u2014 two in New Mexico, one in the Yucat\u00e1n. 59	      "page_level_design_instruction": "## Home Page — Lava Mouth Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Narrative Arc
The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. 111	      "page_level_design_instruction": "## Our Story — Page-Level Design Direction

### Page Role & Emotional Arc
This is the editorial heart of the Lava Mouth site. Where the Home page arrives with a shout, the Story page earns its place by slowing down just enough to feel human — then building back to a warm, confident close. The scroll should feel like reading a great short story: deliberate pacing, a few genuine surprises, and a payoff that makes you want to buy the sauce. Every section has a distinct skeleton; no two layouts repeat the same structure.

### Section Sequence & Rhythm
1. **Page Header** — Cinematic, near-full-viewport stillness. Dense typographic moment. Sparse layout, maximum weight.
2. **Story Block (Founding)** — Warm editorial prose with a large Memphis illustration dominating the left half. The first human, slow-down moment.
3. **Timeline** — The page's highest-energy structural section. Alternating teal and yellow color blocks, bold oversized year numerals, zigzag milestone rhythm. Kinetic and celebratory.
4. **Story Block (Philosophy)** — A manifesto-style section built around a bold pull-quote typographic stunt and an illustrated sourcing map. Confident and grounded.
5. **CTA Close** — Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Warm, personal, handshake energy. Centered composition (the one justified exception on this page — the editorial close demands it).

### Signature Moment
**The Timeline's Oversized Year Numerals as Color-Block Anchors (Section 3).** Each milestone year is rendered in Boogaloo at ~160–180px, all-caps weight, filled with alternating Jalapeño Teal and Habanero Yellow, and bleeds slightly off the left edge of its block — functioning simultaneously as a structural divider, a decorative Memphis graphic element, and the actual content label. The year numeral IS the section header, not a label above it. This move is unmistakably Memphis: bold flat color, oversized type used as shape, and the deliberate off-grid bleed that creates structural tension. It could not exist on a SaaS or heritage page.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As each timeline block enters the viewport, its oversized year numeral slides in from the left — starting off-screen, landing with a slight elastic overshoot — while the milestone text fades up a beat later. The alternating teal/yellow blocks themselves scale up from 95% to 100% as they arrive, giving the section a rhythmic, accordion-like energy as the visitor scrolls through the brand's history.

### Color & Surface Logic
- Section 1 (Header): Lava Cream (#FFF5E1) background. Molten Coral headline fill. Smoke Ring Black body.
- Section 2 (Founding Story): Lava Cream surface, large Memphis illustration left. Sauce Bottle Green used on chapter eyebrow pill. Confetti Pink squiggles scattered behind illustration.
- Section 3 (Timeline): Full-bleed alternating blocks — Jalapeño Teal (#00B8A0) and Habanero Yellow (#FFD600) per milestone pair. Year numerals in contrasting palette color (yellow on teal blocks, teal on yellow blocks). Milestone text in Smoke Ring Black.
- Section 4 (Philosophy): Lava Cream surface with a Ghost Pepper Purple (#7B2FBE) pull-quote stripe cutting horizontally across the section. Illustration of the sourcing map placed right. Molten Coral used on the "Flavor First" pull-quote text inside the purple stripe.
- Section 5 (CTA): Ghost Pepper Purple (#7B2FBE) full-bleed panel. Habanero Yellow headline. Lava Cream body text. Molten Coral primary CTA button. Jalapeño Teal secondary CTA button.

### Typography Hierarchy
- H1 (Page Header): Boogaloo, ~88px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream — the arrival statement.
- H2 (Section Headlines): Boogaloo, 52–60px, sentence case, color varies by section surface.
- Pull Quote (Section 4): Boogaloo, ~72px, all-caps, Molten Coral on Ghost Pepper Purple stripe — the typographic stunt.
- Eyebrow Labels: Permanent Marker, 12px, loose tracking, in pill shapes — Confetti Pink background on light surfaces, Habanero Yellow on dark.
- Body: Nunito, 17px, 1.7 line-height, 65ch measure, Smoke Ring Black on light surfaces, Lava Cream on dark panels.
- Timeline Year Numerals: Boogaloo, 160–180px, alternating Habanero Yellow / Jalapeño Teal fills.
- Timeline Milestone Titles: Boogaloo, 28px, Smoke Ring Black.
- Timeline Descriptions: Nunito, 16px, semi-bold 600, Smoke Ring Black.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page breathes through deliberate contrast: the header and philosophy sections are sparse and editorial (generous vertical padding, restrained element count); the timeline section is intentionally dense and energetic (tight stacking, bold color blocks, maximum graphic weight). This alternating dense/sparse rhythm mirrors the storytelling scroll structure — tension and release, just like a good story.

### Motion Design

**On-Load Arc (Page Header):**
- The Lava Cream background arrives instantly.
- The eyebrow pill fades in and drops down from 12px above its resting position.
- A beat later, the H1 headline ("It Started With a Pepper Plant and a Dare") reveals word by word, each word sliding up from 20px below with a quick, snappy ease — the Molten Coral fill appearing as each word lands.
- The subheadline fades in as a unit a beat after the last headline word settles.
- Three small Confetti Pink Memphis squiggle shapes drift in from off-screen corners — one from top-left, one from bottom-right, one from the right edge — each on a slight delay, landing gently behind the text stack.

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 2 (Founding Story): The illustration slides in from the left while the editorial text block fades up from below. The two motions are slightly offset — illustration arrives first, text follows a beat later — so the image "sets the scene" before the words appear.
- Section 3 (Timeline): Each milestone block triggers individually as it enters the viewport. The oversized year numeral slides in from the left with an elastic overshoot (the signature motion moment). The milestone title and description fade up a beat after the numeral lands. Blocks alternate left-to-right entry direction to match the zigzag layout rhythm.
- Section 4 (Philosophy): The Ghost Pepper Purple pull-quote stripe wipes in from left to right — like a highlighter stroke — before the quote text fades in on top of it. The sourcing map illustration scales up from 97% to 100% as it enters, with a gentle fade.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The entire panel fades in and scales from 98% to 100% as it enters. The two CTA buttons stagger in — primary first, secondary a beat later.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- CTA Buttons (Section 5): Primary Molten Coral button lifts 3px, shadow deepens, and the label shifts to Smoke Ring Black on hover. Secondary Jalapeño Teal button gets a 2px Habanero Yellow border highlight and slight lift.
- Timeline milestone blocks: A subtle 2px Molten Coral left border appears on hover, and the milestone title shifts from Smoke Ring Black to Molten Coral.
- All interactive elements receive a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- The three Confetti Pink squiggle decorations in the page header drift very slowly — a gentle, looping float animation (up 6px, back, up 6px) on a ~4-second cycle, each offset so they never move in unison. This gives the header a living, breathing quality without distracting from the headline.
- In Section 3, a thin Confetti Pink dot-pattern strip runs horizontally between the timeline and the section header — this strip slowly scrolls left at a very gentle pace (marquee-style, nearly imperceptible) to suggest forward momentum through the brand's history.

**Signature Motion Moment (named):** "The Year Numeral Slam-In" — as each timeline block enters the viewport, its oversized year numeral (160–180px Boogaloo) launches in from the left edge of the screen, decelerating sharply and overshooting its final position by ~8px before snapping back. The effect feels like a rubber stamp being pressed onto the page — bold, physical, irreverent. This is the kinetic expression of the Memphis aesthetic: type as graphic object, motion as personality.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** Timeline uses a two-column zigzag layout — odd milestones left-aligned, even milestones right-aligned, with the year numeral bleeding off the outer edge. Story blocks use a 55/45 asymmetric split (illustration / text). Pull-quote stripe spans full content width.
- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Timeline collapses to a single left-aligned column with year numerals at 110px. Story block splits become 50/50 stacked if needed, illustration above text. Pull-quote stripe remains full-width.
- **Mobile (below 768px):** All sections stack vertically. Year numerals reduce to 80px but retain their color fills. Illustrations stack above their text blocks. Full-bleed color panels (timeline, CTA) extend edge-to-edge. Typography scales down gracefully — H1 to ~52px, H2 to ~38px, pull quote to ~44px.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses the full palette expressively — Jalapeño Teal and Habanero Yellow dominate the timeline (their designated "alternating color blocks" usage), Ghost Pepper Purple anchors the philosophy pull-quote and CTA close (its designated "testimonial section panels" usage), and Molten Coral carries the hero headline and pull-quote text (its designated "hero headline fills" usage). Boogaloo, Nunito, and Permanent Marker are all deployed at their specified scales. The Memphis visual cues — abstract squiggles, confetti shapes, bright blocks, patterned backgrounds — are structural devices here, not afterthoughts. This page is the most editorial on the site, but it never forgets it belongs to a loud, joyful, irreverent hot sauce brand.",

**Page Role & Goal**
This is the warmest, most human page on the site. It must feel like knocking on a kitchen door and being welcomed in — not submitting a ticket to a help center. The Memphis Playful aesthetic is fully deployed, but dialed toward warmth and invitation rather than pure spectacle. The storytelling scroll structure moves visitors from welcome → self-identification → action → human connection → self-service, each section shifting rhythm and density to prevent monotony.

**Section Sequence & Rhythm**
1. **Page Header** — Full-bleed, loud arrival. Asymmetric type composition, Molten Coral headline fill, confetti shapes scattered across the panel. Dense and energetic.
2. **Feature Grid** — Four inquiry-type cards on a Habanero Yellow background block. Memphis illustration anchors the composition off-center. Grid breaks from the header's full-bleed by introducing contained card forms. Medium density.
3. **Contact Block** — The form. Lava Cream surface, deliberate sparse breathing room. The only quiet moment on the page — stillness signals focus and low friction. Minimal ornament.
4. **Story Block** — Founder note. Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel, white and Habanero Yellow type. Feels like a handwritten letter pinned to a bulletin board. Dense emotionally, sparse structurally. The page's **signature visual moment** lives here (see below).
5. **FAQ** — Jalapeño Teal background, accordion-style stacked questions. Ends with a CTA chip pointing to Stockists. Returns to medium density with bold typographic rhythm.

**Signature Visual Moment**
The **Story Block (Section 4)** is the page's signature moment. The word "DANI" is set in Boogaloo at approximately 160–180px, all-caps, in Habanero Yellow with a Smoke Ring Black outline stroke, running diagonally at a slight upward angle (roughly 6–8°) behind the founder's quote text like a watermark that refuses to be a watermark — it bleeds off the right edge of the panel and partially off the bottom. The founder's body copy sits in Nunito Regular 18px in Lava Cream, left-aligned, overlapping the oversized name. A Confetti Pink squiggle rule separates the eyebrow from the headline. This is unmistakably Memphis: graphic type used as texture, color as contrast anchor, and the irreverent energy of a sauce label applied to a personal founder note. It is not imported from any other aesthetic — it is the logical conclusion of Boogaloo at display scale meeting a saturated full-bleed panel.

**Signature Motion Moment**
Tied to the Story Block: as the section scrolls into view, the oversized "DANI" letterform slides in from the right edge — slowly, over about 700ms — as if the name is arriving late to its own introduction, settling into its diagonal position just as the founder copy fades up. This staggered entrance makes the typographic stunt feel alive and intentional rather than static decoration.

**Color & Surface Logic**
- Section 1 (Header): Lava Cream background, Molten Coral headline, Smoke Ring Black body, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow confetti shapes scattered at large scale.
- Section 2 (Feature Grid): Habanero Yellow full-bleed background panel, cards in Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text, Molten Coral card-top accent bars, Jalapeño Teal email links.
- Section 3 (Contact Form): Lava Cream background, Ghost Pepper Purple form field labels, Molten Coral submit button, Jalapeño Teal focus rings on inputs.
- Section 4 (Story Block): Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed background, Habanero Yellow oversized "DANI" type, Lava Cream body copy, Confetti Pink squiggle rule, Sauce Bottle Green eyebrow pill.
- Section 5 (FAQ): Jalapeño Teal background, Lava Cream accordion rows, Smoke Ring Black question text, Habanero Yellow open/close chevron icons, Molten Coral CTA chip.

**Typographic Hierarchy**
- H1 (Section 1): Boogaloo 80–90px, Molten Coral fill, sentence case, tight tracking.
- H2 (Sections 2, 3, 4, 5): Boogaloo 52–60px, color varies by section surface.
- Eyebrows: Permanent Marker 12–13px, loose tracking, on pill backgrounds matching section accent.
- Body: Nunito 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, Regular or Semi-bold 600 for intros.
- Form labels: Nunito Semi-bold 600, 14px, Ghost Pepper Purple.
- FAQ questions: Nunito Bold 700, 18px, Smoke Ring Black on Lava Cream rows.
- Oversized "DANI" watermark: Boogaloo ~170px, Habanero Yellow, Smoke Ring Black outline, diagonal.

**Density & Whitespace Logic**
The page alternates between dense/energetic (Sections 1, 2, 4) and sparse/focused (Sections 3, 5). Section 3 is the page's quietest moment — generous padding (100px top/bottom), maximum 640px form width centered, no decorative ornament — so the form feels approachable, not buried. Section 5 returns to medium density with the accordion rhythm.

**Motion Design — Full Arc**
- **On-load (Section 1):** The Molten Coral headline ("We're Real People Who Really Love Hot Sauce") slides up from 24px below its final position and fades in over ~500ms. A beat after it settles, the subheadline fades up. Then, the confetti shapes (Confetti Pink circles, Habanero Yellow triangles, Jalapeño Teal squiggles) pop in one by one in a staggered sequence — each shape scaling from 0 to full size with a slight bounce — over about 800ms total. The eyebrow pill slides in from the left before the headline arrives.
- **Scroll-triggered reveals:** Each section's headline and body stagger-fade up (translate Y 20px → 0, opacity 0 → 1) as they enter the viewport via IntersectionObserver. Section 2 cards stagger in left-to-right with a 100ms delay between each card. Section 5 FAQ rows stagger in top-to-bottom.
- **Hover affordances:** Feature grid cards (Section 2) lift 5px with a deepened Smoke Ring Black box shadow and the top accent bar shifts from Molten Coral to Jalapeño Teal on hover. Email links in cards underline-grow from left on hover. The "Send It" submit button scales to 1.04 and shifts background from Molten Coral to Ghost Pepper Purple on hover. FAQ accordion rows show a Habanero Yellow left border (4px) on hover before click. The "Find a Stockist" CTA chip in Section 5 fills with Molten Coral on hover with white text.
- **Ambient looped motion:** The confetti shapes in Section 1 have a slow, continuous floating drift — each shape independently oscillating 6–8px up and down on a staggered sine-wave loop (roughly 3–4 second cycles, offset per shape) so the header feels alive without being distracting. The Memphis illustration in Section 2 (open envelope with chili pepper) has a very subtle slow rotation oscillation — ±3° over a 4-second loop — like it's gently breathing.
- **Signature motion moment:** As Section 4 (Story Block) enters the viewport, the oversized "DANI" letterform slides in from the right edge over ~700ms with an ease-out curve, settling into its diagonal position behind the copy. A half-beat later, the founder body copy fades up from 16px below. The Confetti Pink squiggle rule draws in left-to-right (width animates from 0 to full) just before the headline arrives. Together these three moves create a layered cinematic reveal that makes the signature moment feel earned.

**Responsive Behavior**
- Mobile (< 640px): Section 1 headline drops to 52px, confetti shapes reduce in count and scale. Section 2 cards stack to single column. Section 3 form goes full-width with 24px horizontal padding. Section 4 oversized "DANI" scales to ~90px and shifts to horizontal (non-diagonal) to remain legible at small widths. Section 5 accordion goes full-width single column.
- Tablet (640–1024px): Section 2 cards go 2×2 grid. Section 4 maintains diagonal treatment at reduced scale (~120px). All other sections maintain single-column centered with generous side padding.
- Desktop (> 1024px): Full compositions as described above, max-width container ~1280px centered.

**Fit Within Shared Design System**
This page uses every palette color at least once, deploys Boogaloo at multiple display scales, uses Permanent Marker for all eyebrow pills, and uses Nunito for all body and form text. It is the most restrained page in the set (the form section is genuinely quiet) while still being unmistakably Lava Mouth. The signature moment (oversized diagonal "DANI" in the Ghost Pepper Purple panel) is the loudest single typographic gesture on any page in the site, which is appropriate for the final page of a storytelling scroll — it ends with a human name, not a product shot.",
